issues.claim: "one free Weebly page" (header, and "free Weebly page" in the source list)
issues.problem: The page is served from hugheslaw.weebly.com with a 'Powered by Weebly' signup footer and no custom domain, which supports but does not prove the free plan tier. The tier is never stated on the page.
issues.fix: Say "a Weebly site on a free subdomain with no custom domain" rather than asserting the plan tier.

issues.claim: "rented suites in two towns" (header and source list)
issues.problem: The site publishes two suite addresses (Suite 204, Little Silver Prof'l Plaza; 4G Auer Court, 2d Floor, Williamsburg Commons) but says nothing about ownership or tenancy. "Rented" is an inference (small numbered suites in multi-tenant professional buildings) presented as fact.
issues.fix: Use "suites in two towns" in the body and label the leased-suite reading as an inference if kept.

issues.claim: Section 1 impact "104-208 staff hours a year ... at $37.91/hour (legal-secretary median)" and Section 2 "16-40 staff hours"
issues.problem: This practice has one attorney and no staff anywhere in its footprint, so hours saved at a legal-secretary rate are a proxy, not a cash saving the firm currently bears. The arithmetic is correct; the framing is loose.
issues.fix: State that this is the value of the typing time currently done by the attorney (or of a hire avoided), or price the first two estimates at the lawyer rate and keep the secretary rate only as a low-end floor.

issues.claim: "52 weeks x 2-4 hours x all of that typing automated" and Section 3 "x all of that time handled" (100% automation)
issues.problem: A 100% capture rate contradicts the audit's own sign-off model ("anything filed, quoted or sent waits for your sign-off") and the review time that implies, so the top of each range is optimistic even though the assumptions are disclosed.
issues.fix: Apply a stated capture rate (e.g. 60-70%) or add "before the attorney's review time" to each figure.

issues.claim: "Compliance lists, not discipline findings; a listed attorney is not allowed to practise."
issues.problem: Accurately quoted from the NJ good-standing definitions and correctly framed as administrative, but the audit does not note that the lists are dated snapshots and that a later reinstatement notice may exist (the 2026 list runs to 9 November 2026).
issues.fix: Add half a sentence: current status should be confirmed against the court's good-standing record before any engagement.
